exposure: Pregnancies with active SLE at conception vs. inactive SLE at conception
Pregnancies with lupus nephritis vs. without nephritis
cohort: 115 pregnancies in 86 women with SLE over a 10-year period (2006-2015)
finding: Lupus pregnancies remain high-risk pregnancies with significant maternal and foetal complications, particularly for those with active SLE at conception and those with antiphospholipid syndrome.
mod_finding: 45.1% of the women in the study underwent caesarean sections.
